edits.file: internal/settings/ (regen step) / dispatch-shape note in the plan
edits.edit: Resolve the ownership collision: the internal/hookspec/hookspec.go edit instructs the Go implementer lane to run `go test ./internal/settings -run TestRenderGolden -update` and `make install`, while the separate dispatch-shape paragraph assigns 'the settings golden regen' to the concurrent sonnet test agent in the SAME message. Pick one owner (recommend the Go implementer, since the golden regen can only run correctly after hookspec.go is actually edited, and it is unrelated to the test agent's lint_test.go/workflowlint_test.go scope).
edits.why: Two concurrently-dispatched agents both touching internal/settings/testdata/settings.golden.json and running `make install` risks a race or duplicated work, and CLAUDE.md hard rule 1 treats settings.json regeneration as a single deliberate step.

edits.edit: Add an explicit decision, documented in meta or in the plan's Not-doing list, on whether implement-and-verify chains into audit-fix-verify (e.g. `workflow('audit-fix-verify', {paths: gate.filesChanged, cwd, refuters: LEGS_OK})`) once its own gate-loop returns green, or is intentionally exempt from goal clause 2's recursive re-audit requirement.
edits.why: GOAL point (2) groups audit-fix-verify / implement-and-verify / gate-loop together under 'the loop recursively re-audits what it just fixed... until dry or capped,' but the plan only adds real fix-then-re-audit recursion to audit-fix-verify; implement-and-verify still runs exactly one implement pass + one gate-loop call with no stated justification for the gap.

edits.edit: Add one example call per named role from the GOAL text that isn't otherwise demonstrated, e.g. `workflow('vendor-leg', {leg:'copilot', task:'stage and commit <files>'})` for the 'copilot commit' role, and a one-line note on invoking leg:'gemini' for a 1M-context sweep stage.
edits.why: GOAL clause 3 names specific per-leg roles ('codex adversarial verify, gemini 1M sweep, copilot commit, opencode'), but the plan wires only codex as a default refuter; vendor-leg.js is generic and no script/doc shows how a caller would actually use it for the other three named roles, even though 'Not doing' only explains why they're off by default, not how to turn them on for those roles.

edits.edit: Either remove or comment the unreachable ': error' arm in the new `exit` ternary (`last.status === 'green' ? 'green' : stalled ? 'stalled' : history.length === MAX_ITER ? 'capped' : 'error'`) — given the loop's own break conditions, any time execution reaches that third arm, history.length is necessarily === MAX_ITER, so ': error' can never actually be returned from gate-loop's own return statement.
edits.why: CLAUDE.md simplicity rule: no handling for impossible states. This is a correctness/clarity nit, not a functional bug — low severity — but worth a one-line comment explaining why 'error' never surfaces here (it would come from the agent call returning null, already normalized to status:'error' upstream, not from this ternary branch).

edits.file: GOAL/Part B narrative text (not a file edit, a wording fix in the plan itself)

Replace with budget math that matches the code: smoke ≤3m + task ≤3m ≤ 6m, safely under the Bash tool's 10-minute ceiling.
edits.why: Internal contradiction between the plan's own narrative justification and the vendor-leg.js code/prompt it describes — would confuse whoever implements or later reads the whenToUse rationale.
